0.translation: Each map retains all source features, independent reference primers and every site in its declared enzyme profile. No three-site sampling is used. Maps use their own complete sequence, the same layers and a 10 × 8 in canvas. Open the full-resolution image for annotation text.

4.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧, ⟦shared:1⟧ and ⟦shared:2⟧ are the complete tables submitted to the plot. ⟦shared:3⟧ retains raw matches; ⟦shared:4⟧ identifies the enzyme profile. Feature geometry is not thinned and the site profile is not sampled to a fixed count.

47.translation: Saved reference profiles take priority within ⟦shared:0⟧. The pETDuet-1 file saves None while its reference PNG shows sites, so ⟦shared:1⟧ is selected explicitly. This does not claim to recover the original PNG export settings. Every row of the chosen profile is retained. Complete means that declared profile, rather than every candidate from every enzyme database on one map.

48.translation: Independent primers use ⟦shared:0⟧. A source without independent reference primers has zero such rows; no records are invented. Named pieces remain in ⟦shared:1⟧ rather than becoming new top-level features. Enzymes at a shared position can share a label while their input records remain available.
